source_note: gland dims from Palmetto catalog dash tables (inches -> mm); checks COMPUTED

radial.series: Palmetto 230 (helical, 17-7 PH or Elgiloy), dash -032, jacket 01 virgin PTFE

face.series: Palmetto 239 internal face (helical), dash -026, jacket 01 virgin PTFE
face.note: cold, the PTFE ring shrinks about 0.264 mm more in radius than the Al groove, so it moves off the OD wall that internal pressure pushes it against; the axial spring load still seals the faces, but the cold radial fit (seal OD vs gland OD) must be sized by the supplier for 90 K (K p.4: heavy springs).

surfaces.hardness: HRC 30 min on the dynamic bore (P p.4, C p.18); Al 6061-T6 is far softer -> hard surface or a stainless sleeve; choice and LOX compatibility to confirm with the seal supplier (ASSUMPTION)

verdict: Both seals have catalog glands within ~0.7 mm of the current CAD. Option A (keep 0.10 mm, warm B before mate) stays inside the 0.43 mm diametral limit in every hot/cold case; option B (0.15 mm) never jams but its worst gap exceeds the 10 MPa limit, which is only acceptable if the supplier rates it at our lower pressure.

sleeve.note: ASSUMPTION 17-4 contraction represented by SS304; actual fit stress and bore distortion require thermal FEA

seat_retention.retention: four M1.2 screws + axial hard-stop retainer + load collar, A and B
seat_retention.load_model: ASSUMPTION constant catalog rate at 90K; SS304 contraction proxy for spring; no creep/pressure qualification
